name: Boxwork ridge crest
why: Boxwork ridges are read as old fractures filled and cemented by minerals from groundwater. Sample the crest to compare its cement with the host bedrock.
source: MOCK: placed on mock terrain by pipeline/mock.py

name: Ridge-hollow contact
why: Moving from ridge into hollow shows whether minerals change away from the fracture, a record of how far the fluids soaked into the bedrock.
source: MOCK: placed on mock terrain by pipeline/mock.py

name: Sandy hollow floor
why: Sand in the hollows is the hazard Curiosity's drivers watched for (wheel slip). Trench it and measure grain size and depth to ground-truth the trafficability map.
source: MOCK: placed on mock terrain by pipeline/mock.py

name: Scarp exposure
why: The wall cuts a vertical section through the layered sulfate-bearing bedrock the boxwork formed in. Image and measure the layers from its foot.
source: MOCK: placed on mock terrain by pipeline/mock.py

name: Mock drill site A
why: Stand-in for a Curiosity drill site to revisit. A crew can core deeper than the rover's few-centimetre drill holes and bring the cores home.
source: MOCK: placed on mock terrain by pipeline/mock.py

name: Boulder field float rocks
why: Boulders are float rock shed from layers upslope. Sampling several gives a quick survey of rock types not exposed along the route.
source: MOCK: placed on mock terrain by pipeline/mock.py
